layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 5 congressional districts — the largest districts Connecticut carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 5 features for Connecticut, measured 2026-11-12. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 5 districts (every intersection-over-union 1.0), so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Planning Region
layers.rank_note: 9 planning regions, the Census Bureau's county equivalents for Connecticut, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which planning region (Connecticut's county equivalent) contains the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 9 features, measured 2026-11-12: the nine planning regions the Census Bureau has filed as Connecticut's county equivalents since 2022, in place of its eight former counties. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: Connecticut has had no county government since 1960. Each planning region is a council of governments whose board is made up of the chief elected officials of its towns, and nobody is elected to it directly, so the card says so and points to the Town card.

layers.label: Connecticut Senate District
layers.rank_note: 36 Senate districts, each electing one senator

source.answers: The Senate district covering the point, and the senator it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 36 features, measured 2026-11-12, identical to the 2024 vintage (layer 5) that day. The chambers do not nest, so this map is simplified on its own. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ct-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the General Assembly's own member list as the state publishes it on data.ct.gov (dataset rgw6-bpst): each senator's name, party, Legislative Office Building room and telephone, the General Assembly e-mail address where the list gives one (11 of 36 on 2026-11-12) and page. The query names the columns it reads, so the list's home-address columns are never fetched.

layers.label: School District (Secondary)
layers.rank_note: 8 secondary districts, about 267 km2 of land on average, running the higher grades over part of the elementary districts' ground, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The secondary school district covering the point, where one runs the higher grades over the point's elementary district.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 1 (secondary school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 8 features for Connecticut, measured 2026-11-12: 5 running grades 7 to 12 and 3 running 9 to 12. The unified districts and the elementary districts together cover the state's land (9,113 and 3,429 km2 of Connecticut's 12,542 km2), and the 8 secondary districts lie over part of the elementary districts' ground (2,136 km2), so a reader there is in one elementary and one secondary district at once. One unified record is not a district: the Census files Long Island Sound, where no school district reaches, as "School District Not Defined" (GEOID 0999997, 1,096 km2 of water and no land), and the card says no school district is defined there.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap ct-school-board-members.
source.applies: Connecticut — part of the elementary districts' ground; the layer answers nothing elsewhere.

layers.label: Town
layers.rank_note: 169 towns, about 74 km2 of land on average, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 174 features for Connecticut, measured 2026-11-12: 149 towns, 20 towns the Census records as consolidated with the city or borough of the same name (one government each), and 5 records of coastal water named "County subdivisions not defined". Every part of the state's land is in one of its 169 towns, each a general-purpose government over its whole ground, so this layer is the state's whole municipal map. Nine boroughs and the city of Groton have governments of their own inside their towns; they are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Connecticut's first selectmen, mayors and councils was read in this pass; the card names the town and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap ct-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 288 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Connecticut (470 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Connecticut (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='09'. The app's box reaches into New York, Massachusetts and Rhode Island, and measured 2026-11-12, 288 of the 470 ZCTAs in it reach into Connecticut and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Connecticut. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 162 points in Connecticut's envelope, which reaches into New York, Massachusetts and Rhode Island; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Connecticut — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Connecticut State Capitol, 210 Capitol Avenue, Hartford, Capitol Planning Region

negative_point.note: The Atlantic about 25 km south of Block Island and 30 km south-east of Montauk Point — outside Connecticut and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names no state here (control: the State Capitol returns Connecticut), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does, nor any of the other batch-3 states' outlines. IT IS OPEN WATER, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Connecticut outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (9 planning regions).
Connecticut's 9 planning regions (its county equivalents) — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 5 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same map as layer 4 (CD119).
The 36 Connecticut Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper).
The 151 Connecticut House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Connecticut elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from ct/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
